newsitem.title: USA: ITT Corp. sells rest of Alcatel stake.
newsitem.headline: ITT Corp. sells rest of Alcatel stake.

text.p: ITT Corp., owner of Sheraton hotels and Caesar casinos, said Monday it sold its remaining 4.5 million shares in French telecommunications firm Alcatel Alsthom to an unidentified U.S. institutional investor for approximately $530 million .
The sale was ITT's latest move to divest non-core assets as it tries to fend off a $6.5 billiion hostile takeover bid from Hilton Hotels Corp.
ITT said the sale, which is expected to close April 10,
represented a gain of more than 25 percent over the book value of the stake.

In February, ITT sold nearly half of its 5 percent stake in Alcatel to an unidentified U.S. investment fund for about $300 million. An ITT spokesman would not comment on whether the same buyer was acquiring both portions of the Alcatel stake.
The shares originally were not to be sold before July 3, but Alcatel granted ITT permission to sell its holdings before that date.
The sale of the Alcatel shares had been viewed as a relatively simple step for ITT and was not considered to be one of its most significant asset sales.
Hilton launched its cash and stock offer for ITT in January. ITT rejected the $55 per share bid and announced a plan to sell non-core assets in order to focus on its key hotel and casino businesses.
Other than the Alcatel stake, ITT also has announced plans to sell its 50 percent stake in Madison Square Garden to partner Cablevision Systems Corp. for $650 million.
Other assets to be sold include ITT's international telephone directories unit and an educational services business.

ITT has not disclosed how it will use the proceeds from the asset sales. It said Monday that it will "carefully examine how the proceeds from this (Alcatel) sale and the sale of other non-core assets can best be used to add value for shareholders."
Wall Street analysts have said ITT may authorise a stock buyback or issue a special dividend to keep its shareholders happy.
Shares of ITT fell 25 cents to $58.875 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
